## TL;DR

Unified the product description across every in-repo surface named by the task. npm now carries the long approved line; the landing meta/OpenGraph/Twitter tags and the VitePress site description carry the short hook; the board PWA manifest description no longer uses "task tracking"; and the incidental taglines in the landing hero eyebrow, README, docs homepage, agent Skill, skill reference, and generated `llms.txt` now align with the approved positioning. The retired phrases are gone from product-description copy (`tech leads`, `task tracking`, the npm description's `monorepo`). Landing and docs builds pass, and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` is green. The GitHub "About" text and the Homebrew tap formula are external to this repo and remain human follow-ups.

## Work and rationale

The task supplied two approved strings and told me to use them verbatim:

- Long: `The repo is the operating system. Your AI dev team, living in your repo, for CTOs and builders.`
- Short hook: `Your AI dev team, living in your repo, for CTOs and builders.`

I treated those as the source of truth and mapped each surface to one of them:

- `package.json` `description` → Long. This is the npm landing copy, so it needs the full positioning sentence plus the "repo is the operating system" frame.
- `landing/index.html` meta description, `og:description`, `twitter:description` → Short hook. SEO/social cards have a length limit, and the short hook is the approved SEO line.
- `user-docs/.vitepress/config.mts` `description` → Short hook. That value also feeds the generated docs `llms.txt`, so the docs agent index inherits the same line.
- `src/server/routes/ui.ts` PWA manifest `description` → `${name} · RepoOS`. The task explicitly says this field is not product marketing and only needs "task tracking" removed; the suggested template is the least surprising replacement.
- Landing hero eyebrow `For engineers and tech leads` → `For CTOs and builders`. This is product copy above the fold, so it is part of the positioning change even though the task's file table did not name `landing/src/App.vue`.
- README opening tagline → Long, and the following paragraph's "inside your monorepo" → "inside your repo". The latter was the remaining product-description hit for "monorepo" after the named surfaces were changed.
- Docs homepage tagline → Short hook. The hero headline already says "The repo is the operating system.", so the tagline now carries the audience line.
- `agent/skill/SKILL.md`, `agent/skill/references/what-repoos-does.md`, and the landing `llms.txt` blockquote → prepended the Short hook to the existing functional explanation. The explanation still tells an outside agent what RepoOS does; only the positioning sentence changed.
- npm `keywords`: replaced `monorepo` with `git`. Keywords are published metadata and the retired word was still visible on the package page, so leaving it contradicted the goal even though the acceptance criterion only calls out the description field.

I deliberately did not rewrite longer body copy ("Bring your own agents and models…", the docs feature cards, or the landing page's explanatory paragraphs). The task says to leave that alone unless it sits in a meta/tagline field being replaced. I also left technical uses of "monorepo" in configuration and check documentation, source comments, and test names — those describe real behavior (a monorepo step can target `backend/`), not product positioning. Editing them would have been a misleading mass rewrite.

No test assertions depended on the old strings. The `landingllms` fixture in `agent-file-build-checks.test.ts` is synthetic and independent of the real `renderLlmsTxt()` output, and the PWA icon tests assert icon structure rather than the manifest description. The landing build's own agent-file check verifies that `dist/llms.txt`, install commands, and the shared starter prompt agree; it passed with the new blockquote.

## Approaches tried

I first ran a repo-wide case-insensitive search for the three retired phrases and classified every hit rather than editing mechanically. That separated product copy (npm description, landing meta, docs meta, PWA manifest, landing eyebrow, README opening, docs homepage, Skill copy, `llms.txt`) from legitimate technical references (check configuration, worktree candidate guidance, source comments, tests for monorepo support) and from task/story records under `work/`, `inputs/`, and `stories/`, which are historical records and out of bounds.

For the two site builds I installed each standalone project's dependencies and ran its own build command, because `repoos check` builds the main app but does not build `landing/` or `user-docs/`. Both builds also run their own content checks, so those passed too. I inspected the emitted `landing/dist/index.html`, `landing/dist/llms.txt`, `user-docs/.vitepress/dist/index.html`, and `user-docs/.vitepress/dist/llms.txt` to confirm the approved strings survived the build transformations.

The first scoped check failed only on `check-fmt`: oxfmt wanted the now-short VitePress description on one line. I ran `bun run fmt`, re-ran the scoped check, and it passed. RepoOS created WIP checkpoint commits during those runs, which is expected for this workflow; I did not commit or push anything myself.

## Challenges and blockers

The main judgement call was scope. The acceptance criterion says `rg -i "tech leads|task tracking|monorepo"` should return no product-description hits, not no hits at all. A literal repo-wide removal would have rewritten accurate technical documentation about monorepo support and touched unrelated task history. I kept those and removed only the product-facing uses.

The Homebrew formula and GitHub repository "About" text cannot be changed from this worktree. The formula lives in the separate `repo-os/homebrew-tap` repository, and the About text is repository metadata. The task explicitly defers both to the human, so I did not claim them. Consequently I could not run `brew audit`; that belongs with the tap change. The formula's `desc` field is constrained by Homebrew's style rules, but the short hook is comfortably short enough to keep verbatim when the tap is updated.

One incidental point worth recording: the docs build emits `The repo is the operating system.` as the `llms.txt` blockquote (from the homepage hero) and the short hook as the description line. Both are approved copy, so this is consistent, but it means the docs agent index shows the Long line's first sentence before the short hook rather than the full Long line. That is a template behavior, not content drift.

## Key learnings

- The approved copy already contains the strongest existing sentence ("The repo is the operating system."), so most of this change was choosing which approved line fits which surface rather than inventing new wording.
- Build-time generated files matter: the docs `llms.txt` description comes from the VitePress config, and the landing `llms.txt` comes from a TypeScript template literal. Editing only the visible markdown would have left those stale.
- A phrase sweep needs classification. "Monorepo" is retired as positioning but still correct in technical docs about multi-package check steps; treating every hit as copy would degrade real documentation.
- The repo's own gate builds the main app, not the standalone sites. Acceptance criteria that say "landing builds" and "docs build" need those builds run explicitly, and their emitted output inspected.
